findings.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:137 — The test never synchronizes with the reader (no start barrier or join), so it can pass before any concurrent request runs or finishes.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before its in-flight request records the concurrent-access failure.

tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The test never waits for the reader to start or finish, so it can assert an empty exception list without exercising any concurrent read or before a failing read records its error.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before its in-flight request records the concurrent-access failure.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while `deletedAll.get()` is false, collecting exceptions. After deleting all groups, it sets `deletedAll.set(true)` and immediately asserts `caughtExceptions` is empty. However, the reader thread is never joined - it could still be executing a request when the assertion runs, or could record an exception after the assertion. This is a race condition that could cause the test to pass incorrectly (missing a concurrent-access failure) or fail intermittently. The finding correctly identifies that the thread should be joined before asserting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The test never waits for the reader to start or finish, so it can assert an empty exception list without exercising any concurrent read or before a failing read records its error.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while !deletedAll.get(), but there's no synchronization to ensure the reader thread has started before the main thread begins deleting groups. The main thread could delete all groups and set deletedAll.set(true) before the reader thread even enters its while loop, meaning zero concurrent reads occur. Additionally, after setting deletedAll.set(true), the test immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the reader thread, so any exception thrown in the final iteration might not be recorded yet. This is a real concurrency bug in the test logic.
